subject: HarborPay service disruption - RCA readout & verification checklist
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake@harborpay.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborpay.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Initial notification: HarborPay inference error observed

Jake —

Thank you for flagging the issues this morning. We saw a spike in 5xx errors and token delays for the HarborPay production model group starting ~10:37 UTC. Our on-call runbook triggered automatic failover to the secondary pool at 10:45 UTC and error rates dropped, but some requests experienced degraded responses during the flare.

We are running a full forensic and will share a timeline and immediate mitigations by EOD PST. For transparency we will include logs, the KV-cache snapshot, and our initial hypothesis.

Immediate next steps for this thread:
- We will provide a technical timeline + RCA summary in a follow-up email.
- If you need rollback or additional credits while we investigate, let me know and I will escalate.

Apologies for the disruption. We understand this impacts payment flows and are prioritizing HarborPay.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial notification: HarborPay inference error observed

Team —

Quick internal note while we prepare the customer readout: preliminary findings from runtime traces show sustained KV cache eviction that correlated with peak token churn. We also saw an autoscaler race where two nodes simultaneously attempted to rehydrate the same model shard which resulted in transient 503s.

Irene: can you confirm whether the shard rehydration change we shipped last month could alter eviction timing? Marissa: please coordinate the customer-facing RCA deck and include a clear verification checklist.

I'll attach the raw trace snippet for the SRE review.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake@harborpay.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborpay.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: HarborPay: RCA readout and next steps (timeline + actions)

Jake / Marta —

Below is the concise RCA readout and the verification steps we propose. We've attached a PDF with the full timeline and a remediation checklist. Please review and tell us if you'd like a synchronous call for walk-through.

Summary (what happened)
- At 10:37:12 UTC on 2027-11-29, a combination of elevated per-user prompt branching and a scheduled background reindex for HarborPay caused rapid token sequence growth across a subset of clients.
- Continuous-batching logic produced larger-than-expected batches which triggered aggressive KV-cache eviction under the configured LRU policy.
- During cache rehydration, two autoscaler workers attempted concurrent shard rehydration, which resulted in transient model-serving unavailability for ~8 minutes for ~2% of requests.

Immediate impact
- Average p95 latency spiked from 180ms to 2.8s for affected routes.
- 5xx error rate peaked at 3.2% (baseline <0.02%).
- Payment-authorize requests retried by client SDKs; some payments experienced additional latency but we saw no transaction data loss.

Root causes (contributing)
1) Workload spike coinciding with a background reindex (operational timing mismatch).
2) LRU cache policy not tuned for high burst churn on sequences with long token variance.
3) Autoscaler race condition when rehydrating cold shards (we shipped a scheduler optimization last month that unintentionally increased concurrency for shard rehydration).

Actions delivered (what we did during containment)
- Rolled back scheduler optimization on affected Dedicated pool at 10:50 UTC (automatic failover had already reduced errors).
- Increased KV cache size for HarborPay model group and temporarily relaxed eviction aggressiveness.
- Applied a short-lived request-queue backpressure rule to limit peak batch sizes.

Planned corrective actions (timeline)
- 2027-12-01: Permanent fix for autoscaler race (distributed rehydration lock) deployed to staging.
- 2027-12-03: LRU policy update and workload-adaptive cache heuristics to be validated in canary.
- 2027-12-07: Customer verification window; we will run controlled load tests with HarborPay's QA team.

Verification checklist for HarborPay (what we need from you)
- Approve a 60-minute maintenance window for canary validation (preferred: 2027-12-03 14:00–15:00 UTC).
- Provide a short list of production request patterns you care most about (3–5 representative flows).
- Confirm if HarborPay legal wants the timeline artifacts (logs + redacted traces) delivered to legal@harborpay.com.

Attachments: harborpay_rca_summary.pdf; timeline-logs-20271129.csv; remediation-checklist.xlsx

If you prefer a call to review the document, I'm available tomorrow at 09:30 or 13:00 PST.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
From: Jake Reynolds <jake@harborpay.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HarborPay: RCA readout and next steps (timeline + actions)

Irene / Logan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the checklist. Appreciate the quick rollback and the temporary mitigations. Two quick asks:
1) Can you provide the redacted trace for the user flow that caused the spike (we need it for our internal audit)?
2) We want the canary window on 2027-12-03 at 14:00 UTC — Marta will share the sample flows by tomorrow morning.

We also need confirmation that there will be no chargeback exposure due to retries. Can you loop in billing if that becomes relevant?

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Reynolds
Head of Platform, HarborPay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Reynolds <jake@harborpay.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@harborpay.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HarborPay: RCA readout and next steps (timeline + actions)

Jake / Marta —

Confirmed: we will deliver a redacted trace bundle to legal@harborpay.com by EOD today and will include a short note describing retention scope. I've looped in Billing (cc'd on the separate thread) to review any potential compensation for retries; preliminary assessment indicates no systemic transaction losses and our standard incident credits policy will apply if necessary.

For the canary on 2027-12-03 14:00 UTC: Marina from our SRE team will run the validation and share live metrics; we will also provide a rollback playbook in the event we observe regressions.

Action items assigned:
- Redwood (Irene & SRE): deliver canary runbook and monitoring dashboard by 2027-12-02.
- HarborPay (Marta): provide representative flows by 2027-12-01 12:00 UTC.
- Redwood (Marissa): upload redacted traces + evidence bundle to the shared Drive and notify legal.

Appreciate the collaboration — we know reliability is critical for payment flows and we'll keep you informed during the verification window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
